board.title: Label line states
board.heading: LabelLine
board.intro: One line of labels for one source, used by a Queue row and by a source in Review (LabelLine.swift → LabelLine; in Swift, nil lead/action = the state’s default, "" = hidden). Every text file that becomes Ready in the queue, from a collector, a drop or the app, gets labels suggested in the background, at most 3 files at a time; the rest show Labels next until a slot frees. Suggested labels are dashed chips (green = already in the vault, peach = new): click × to drop one, + Add to type one, Accept all to confirm. A .md that has its own tags keeps them (from the file, no AI call). A failed suggestion says so with Retry; it retries by itself up to 3 times, then waits for you (Retry, + Add, or Send without labels). A file without labels yet stays out of the batch. PDFs and images get no line. Props: labels (names separated by |, “:new” marks a label not yet in the vault), state, lead (“-” hides it), action (“-” hides it), note, quiet (no × or + Add until hover, as in Review), allowSkip (Send without labels, after 3 failed tries), width.

board.title: Log line states
board.heading: LogLine
board.intro: One line of the live log (batch steps, collector output, package installs, Test runs). Steps are plain words with a quiet status mark: a lime check when done, a spinner while running, a faint ring while waiting, peach for failed or for “waiting for you”. The time shows only when the minute changes. A group folds repeated steps (“Read 22 sources”, “Suggesting labels · 14 of 22” with a thin bar) and opens to one line per file (level 1). A note is the AI’s own short status message, in italics, at most 280 characters. Details adds the raw line under each step: tool and target only (path, line range, the first line of a command), never file contents, tool results or a draft’s text. output lines are script output on the dark terminal surface: stderr in peach with a peach gutter, the command and Distill’s own lines in grey. Swift: LogLine in LiveLog.swift. Props: kind (step | group | note | phase | output), state (done | running | waiting | review | failed), text, time, count, progress (“done/total”), detail, showDetail, stream (stdout | stderr | cmd | system), level (0 | 1), expanded, width.

board.title: Script consent states
board.heading: ScriptConsent
board.intro: The explicit first-run consent for a custom script. Distill runs nothing you have not allowed: a new script waits here, and a script whose content changes (its sha256) is paused until you allow the new version. The allowance belongs to the exact script, not to the collector. No Swift view yet: add ScriptConsent. The allowance covers the script and its package manifest (package.json or requirements.txt), because installing packages runs their authors’ code; changes names what changed. packages (a new script’s manifest) says allowing also installs them, right away. Props: state (ask | changed | allowed), interpreter, source, hash, changes, packages, allowedText, width.

board.title: Script editor states
board.heading: ScriptEditor
board.intro: The Script field of a custom collector’s Edit form (and Add, step 2). The language picker (zsh, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript) sits on top; under it, where the file lives, with Reveal in Finder and Open in editor. A script Distill keeps is a real file in its own folder (~/Library/Application Support/Distill/collectors/scripts/<id>/collector.py), so it can be edited in any editor, backed up and versioned; the app edits that same file. Your own file stays where it is: no code box, Choose… picks another. Changing the language or saving a change asks for your OK again. No Swift view yet: add ScriptEditor. board.title: Packages panel states
board.heading: PackagesPanel
board.intro: Packages for a script Distill keeps: the manifest next to the script (package.json for JavaScript and TypeScript, installed with npm into node_modules/; requirements.txt for Python, installed with pip into .venv/), one status line, and Install. It shows in the Edit form only; at a glance it is one Settings line, and install progress or a failed install shows in the status card, like a run. Packages install when you allow the script (adding it, or allowing a changed manifest), so the collector is ready before its first run; Install runs it again; a run installs first only when packages went missing. A run started during an install waits for it. Output is kept like a run’s (last 64 KB, stopped after 10 minutes). A changed manifest needs your OK first. ⋯ holds Clean reinstall (drops node_modules/ or .venv/ and installs again) and Open in editor. No Swift view yet: add PackagesPanel. Props: manifest, state (none | ready | needsInstall | installing | failed, as the core reports; needsOK while the change waits for your OK), lines (manifest lines, | separated; a leading + marks an added line), output, summary, expanded, width.

board.title: Session replace confirm states
board.heading: SessionReplaceConfirm
board.intro: The one confirmation Distill shows, everywhere, when it would continue in an AI session that no longer exists (system-wide rule, 2026-10-05). It appears right where you acted (Approve, Send reply, Allow, an Ask follow-up, Open in Terminal), says plainly why the session is gone, and that a new session will be used. Continue starts the new session seeded with what that place needs; Cancel changes nothing. The quiet monospace line is the technical reason, for when you want it. Calm on purpose: blue, not a warning, because nothing was lost from your vault. Distill shows it only on positive evidence (the runner said the session is not found, its transcript file is gone, or the batch never started one); any other runner error stays an ordinary error. Swift: SessionReplaceConfirm (SessionReplaceConfirm.swift). Props: place (batch | conversation | terminal), reason (missing | notFound | neverStarted | runnerGone), runner, carries, detail, width.

board.title: Apply progress states
board.heading: ApplyProgress
board.intro: What Review shows after you approve, until every approved file is in your knowledge base (designed 2026-10-05). Five steps, with the live log’s marks: You approved; the AI starting (resuming this batch’s own session); applying through the vault core; Added, with counts taken from the checked plan, never from the AI (“22 source pages, 3 concepts, 1 entity added · 6 pages updated”); and the follow-up, finding actions. These are the batch’s live-log steps (job.step), so Show steps opens the same log in full. A failed step turns peach and says what to do, in the words Review already uses (the vault changed after review, the vault was busy, the session is gone). Finding actions is a follow-up: if it fails, the batch is still added, so it stays a quiet line. A batch the core applies itself (labels, runners without tool permissions) has no AI step. Swift: none yet.
